title: Pause + Return
concept: Turns “I need space” into something connecting, by pairing time apart with a set time to come back — protection, without disappearing.
whenToUse: When either of you is overwhelmed — racing heart, can't think straight, contempt creeping in, wanting to flee or win. Any time it's not calm enough to have an honest conversation.
steps: Say it — “I need a pause.” No explanation needed.
Set a time — pick a return time (20 minutes minimum, 24 hours max): “I'll be ready at ___.”
Step away — calm down (walk, shower, breathe, music). Don't rehearse the argument in your head.
Come back — reconnect at the time you said, even briefly, to prove it's a pause, not a disappearance.
Restart warm — warm up and check it's safe, before going back to “where you left off.”

phrases.text: I’m not leaving you; I just need to calm down.

working: A: “I’m overwhelmed. I need a pause. I’ll be ready at 8:30.” B: “Okay. Thank you for giving a time. I’ll see you at 8:30.” They return at 8:30, even for two minutes, then restart warm.
notWorking: “I need space.” (walks away) “We’ll talk later.” — “Later” isn't a return time, and it can feel like being abandoned. Fix: always give an exact time.
activity: Agree your default length (say, 20 minutes) and your max (24 hours). Write the phrases on this card. Practice once on something low-stakes this week, and actually keep the return time.
warn: If the Green Rule gets broken, stop — use this tool first.
